sources.title: Dash Academy curriculum — module 2 manifest row
What is Dash Platform? prerequisite lesson
What is Dash — Governance and treasury

claims.text: The lesson must teach a practical fit decision and cover fit/non-fit, payments and tokens, usernames and NFTs, Dash versus Credits, privacy, and the DAO, ending with quiz challenge why-build-on-dash.

Platform is a strong fit for consensus-backed structured state, decentralized access, and proof-verifiable queries, but not arbitrary deployed code or queries that do not follow contract-defined indexes.
Dash Core is the payment layer; the network attempts to InstantSend-lock qualifying transactions and ChainLocks make the selected chain unambiguous.
Platform supports configurable fungible tokens with protocol-supported actions including mint, transfer, burn, freeze/thaw, distribution, access control, and direct purchase.
Dash is the Core asset, while Credits are Platform fee-accounting units derived from Dash; the documented conversion is 1 Dash to 100,000,000,000 Credits.
Application tokens are separate developer-configured assets rather than Dash or Credits, even when a configured direct token sale accepts Credits.
DPNS associates human-readable .dash names with Platform identities, whose controller proves control through signed interactions.
Dash Platform NFTs are based on uniquely identified documents and may support ownership transfer, mutability/deletion choices, and integrated purchase behavior.
CoinJoin can improve Core payment privacy through a deliberate non-custodial wallet process; it does not automatically encrypt all Dash transactions or Platform records.
DAPI TLS protects data in transit, while Platform state is replicated and queryable; confidential fields therefore require intentional encryption and key management or off-Platform storage.
The Dash DAO governs the Dash network and treasury through masternode voting on proposal funding; building on Dash does not automatically create application-specific governance.

A sound architecture uses Dash for native settlement or independently verifiable shared identity, state, and assets while retaining other systems for private data, arbitrary computation, and unsupported query workloads.

conflicts.topic: Credits fee model across protocol versions
conflicts.resolution: The lesson states only the stable invariant that Credits are accounting units derived from Dash and used for Platform costs. It does not present the identity-balance flow as the only fee model or broaden into protocol-version fee eras.
